title: Handoff Tenant Policy
description: The deployment-side configuration a server resolves at raise time and snapshots onto each request, so that a policy edit mid-flight cannot retroactively change what happened. Policy governs WHO is reached and HOW LONG we wait. It MUST NOT govern WHETHER a request may be raised, and it MUST NOT be able to force requests into `gated` mode — blocking is a property a request declares, never a policy imposed on a class of actions.

v.description: Envelope version. A server that does not implement the declared version MUST reject the policy and MUST NOT apply it partially (I21).

defaults.description: Applied when a request does not declare its own value. A request MAY raise an authority floor and MUST NOT lower one.

ttl.description: Null means requests do not expire by default. The ask then stands until answered, cancelled, or superseded.

attempt_ttl.description: One attempt window for every capability and every field set. A server MUST NOT vary it by interaction type.

mode.description: Fixed. A deployment MUST NOT default requests to `gated`; that setting would re-create an interception gate, which is outside this protocol.

authority_floors.description: Minimums a request cannot go below. The derived secret-field floor of the specification applies regardless of what is written here.

allow_link_only.description: A server MUST NOT accept auth_strength `link_only` unless this is explicitly true. When it is, the receipt records actor.type = "anonymous_link" and names no principal.

secret_field_min_role.description: Derived, not configurable downward: any request declaring a `secret` field is raised to this role.

routing.description: The escalation ladder. The client declares urgency; the server decides the channel.

ladders.description: Keyed by urgency. A request's declared urgency selects a ladder; the resolved ladder is snapshotted onto the request.

allow_request_override.description: Whether a request may supply its own ladder. Doing so requires a separate scope from raising a request: a key that can ask a question is a different blast radius from one that can page an on-call engineer at 3 a.m.

quiet_hours.description: Windows in which a channel is suppressed rather than attempted. A suppressed delivery is recorded, never silently dropped.

override_urgency.description: The one urgency permitted to break the window, if any.

channels.description: Every registered channel adapter declares what it can prove and whether it can identify a person. These declarations are what keep the core branch-free.

max_grade.description: The highest evidence this channel can produce. A server MUST NOT record a grade above it.

can_authenticate_person.description: False means answers from this channel are provisional and MUST be completed on an answer-capable surface (I6).

requires_binding.description: Whether a channel identity must be verifiably bound to a principal before its answers count. Binding MUST be an act by an already-authenticated person, never an assertion by the channel.

config_ref.description: Opaque adapter configuration reference. Never a credential by value.

callbacks.description: See signing.md. A server MUST support at least two simultaneously active secrets per endpoint so rotation is an overlap, not a cutover.

secret_refs.description: References only. A secret value MUST NOT appear in a policy document.

state.description: An endpoint failing every attempt for 24 hours MUST be disabled and the tenant notified.

grant_ttl.description: Tracks the request's attempt deadline and is renewed whenever the attempt is re-armed.

session_lease.description: Bounds revocation lag and produces the recorded held duration.

max_shared_with.description: The widest blast radius this tenant will auto-page for. This is the one blast-radius field the core compares; everything else in the object is opaque provider text.

record_navigations.description: Granularity of the navigation record. Input content is never recordable at any setting.

retention.description: Receipts are append-only; retention governs how long they are served, never whether they may be altered.

x-extensions.description: Vendor extensions. Stored verbatim, returned verbatim, never interpreted.
